use_case_summary: GlobeLex is building a multilingual legal discovery/search product for EU clients. Primary workload: large-scale document search and compliance discovery using embeddings for candidate generation and a cross-encoder reranker for precision in the top results. Scale: indexing pipeline expected to reach 10-20M documents (PDFs, contracts, court filings) with mixed languages (EN/FR/DE/ES/JP/KO). Latency targets: p95 end-to-end < 400ms for standard queries; interactive UX requires < 200ms for simple lookups. Cost constraints: target cost-per-query below $0.02 average (including embedding + rerank) for high-volume routes; heavy reranker use is the main cost driver. Engineering wants per-language recall baselines (target >90% EN, >85% FR/DE/ES, >80% JA/KO) and an easy way to re-tune thresholds per locale. Preference toward language-agnostic embeddings for candidate generation (XLM-R or multilingual SBERT) to simplify indexing, but open to per-language embedding models if retrieval recall improves. Reranker: cross-encoder on GPU for top-K (K=20) with fallback to cheaper bi-encoder scoring when under load. Operational asks: VPC + customer-managed KMS, SOC2 + ISO27001, long-term audit logs and data residency in EU. Interested in Redwood's Smart routing (region + capacity fallback) and Optimize toolkit for quantization and batching advice.
additional_context: Technical ask summary for SE: recommend serving topology for 15M doc index (replication/sharding), ANN strategy (HNSW vs IVF-PQ tradeoffs for multilingual vectors), quantization knobs to hit cost target, and reranker orchestration pattern (async rerank, top-K tuning). Team will share per-language eval sets. Legal requires contract language for EU data residency; procurement prefers annual reserved capacity with burst options. Client curious about Redwood's fallback policies when Dedicated capacity peaks (auto-fail to hosted variant) and how audit logs surface per-request model version and prompt hash.
